requirements.requirement: PostgreSQL 16 installed and node1 configured as a writable streaming-replication primary (wal_level, max_wal_senders, hot_standby, pg_hba.conf rules, replication role)
requirements.summary: postgresql-server 16.14 installed on node1; postgresql.conf updated with listen_addresses/wal_level/max_wal_senders/hot_standby; pg_hba.conf updated with replication and client-access rules; replicator role created; postgresql restarted and confirmed listening on 0.0.0.0:5432/[::]:5432.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 built as standbys of node1 via base backup and running in continuous recovery
requirements.summary: pg_basebackup -R from node1 succeeded on both nodes producing standby.signal and primary_conninfo; postgresql started and pg_is_in_recovery()=t confirmed on both node2 and node3.

requirements.requirement: Primary sees both standbys actively streaming (functional replication topology)
requirements.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 lists both 10.100.241.11 and 10.100.241.12 in state=streaming; reconfirmed again later in the run.

requirements.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys, and standbys remain read-only
requirements.summary: A row inserted on node1 appeared via SELECT on both node2 and node3 within seconds; direct INSERT attempts on both standbys were rejected with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state for every managed node
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id captured for all three nodes before any restart. node2 and node3 were rebooted first (connection drop observed, new boot_id confirmed, postgresql active and still in-recovery with prior data intact), then primary streaming to both standbys was reconfirmed, then node1 was rebooted last (new boot_id, postgresql active and NOT in recovery, new row inserted post-restart and replicated to both standbys, pg_stat_replication showed both reconnected). All three post-restart boot_ids match the independent after_executor lifecycle snapshot, cross-confirming the transitions were genuine.

overall_summary: The executor successfully configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication with node1 as a writable primary and node2/node3 as read-only standbys built via pg_basebackup. Data propagation from primary to both standbys and standby write-rejection were directly demonstrated. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed correctly in a safe standbys-first, primary-last order, with pre/post boot-identity changes, connectivity drops during reboot, and post-restart verification of service state, recovery role, and data/replication continuity on all three nodes — independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only shortfalls are minor hygiene issues: a leftover plaintext replication password file on node1 and unrevoked cross-node SSH key trust used only to relay that password.
limitations: Only a single pre-existing row plus one post-restart row were used to demonstrate propagation; this is sufficient to show the mechanism works but is a minimal sample.
No test of promoting a standby to primary or of behavior under an unplanned primary outage (not required by the task, but limits insight into failover readiness beyond graceful restarts).
The plaintext replication password file left on node1 (/tmp/repl_pw.txt) and the persistent SSH trust configured between nodes are minor unresolved hygiene items.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were necessary and bounded (package install, firewalld service opening, postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf edits, pg_basebackup, SSH key placement for password transfer). Two residue items were not cleaned up on node1: the plaintext replication-role password file /tmp/repl_pw.txt (chmod 600, created by cmd-d1590dc52c7a40d7) was deleted on node2/node3 (cmd-00c62e8e49e04333) but left in place on node1, visible in the after_executor temp-files snapshot for node1 — a low-risk but avoidable leftover secret. Persistent SSH key trust between all three nodes (cmd-bcf9042630d14699, cmd-cf5c80daf7d54e65, cmd-faab9edbae77458b) was established solely to relay the one-time password and was never revoked, a broader-than-necessary but low-risk residual mutation. Benign installer artifacts (/tmp/install.log, /tmp/install.pid, /tmp/scp_err.log) were also left on all nodes but pose no security concern. No failed services, no destructive actions, and firewalld/package state ended healthy on all nodes.
